description: FILE STATUS '38' reported by the TRNXFILE CLOSE takes the ELSE arm of the guard at app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L862-L868, and this is the ONE case in the twenty whose abend fires AFTER a complete statement has already been written - which makes it the only case where the WRITES channel and the FINAL_STATE channel disagree, and therefore the only place a translation that confused the two can be caught. UNIT AND INVOCATION: statement.StatementGenerationJobA as a BATCH_JOB, reached at step/Tasklet level with statement.StatementGenerationJobB as its constructor-injected collaborator - no JobLauncher, no job repository and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). jobParameters is empty because no step of app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL declares a PARM - the only PARM in this estate is INTCALC.jcl's PARM='2022071800' - and the step that runs this program is STEP040, EXEC PGM=CBSTM03A,COND=(0,NE) at :L79. THE GUARD, VERBATIM, AND THE NINE SITES THAT SHARE IT. 9100-TRNXFILE-CLOSE sets the call up exactly as the source does - MOVE 'TRNXFILE' TO WS-M03B-DD (:L857), SET M03B-CLOSE TO TRUE (:L858), MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC (:L859) - and CALL 'CBSTM03B' USING WS-M03B-AREA (:L860) reports '38'. The guard is then IF WS-M03B-RC = '00' OR '04' (:L862) / CONTINUE (:L863) / ELSE (:L864) / DISPLAY 'ERROR CLOSING TRNXFILE' (:L865) / DISPLAY 'RETURN CODE: ' WS-M03B-RC (:L866) / PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM (:L867) / END-IF (:L868), and EXIT at :L870 is never reached. That two-value acceptance test is this program's OPEN-and-CLOSE convention and it appears at NINE sites: the four opens at :L736, :L771, :L789 and :L807, the four closes at :L862, :L879, :L895 and :L911, and, easily missed, the FIRST TRNXFILE read at :L748 inside 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN, which is a READ that nevertheless uses the OPEN's form. NOT ONE OF THE NINE HAS A '10' ARM, and that asymmetry is deliberate rather than an oversight: end of file is not a meaningful outcome of an open or a close, so on any of these nine sites even '10' would take the ELSE and abend. The read sites are shaped differently and must stay differently shaped - 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT at :L353-:L362 and 8500-READTRNX-READ at :L837-:L847 are ordered three-arm EVALUATEs where '10' is benign, while 2000-CUSTFILE-GET at :L379-:L386 and 3000-ACCTFILE-GET at :L403-:L410 are two-arm EVALUATEs with no '10' arm at all. Unifying them fails in both directions: route a close through a read's three-arm EVALUATE and '10' becomes a successful end of file on a close, which it never is; drop the '04' acceptance and a perfectly successful close abends. The order of the arms is itself the assertion (gate G30), and the '00' OR '04' pair is preserved exactly as written - not narrowed to '00', not widened, and with nothing whatever emitted on '04' (practice B5). THE EIGHT GUARD LITERALS DIFFER ONLY IN VERB AND DD NAME, SO EACH MUST BE PINNED SEPARATELY. The four closes emit 'ERROR CLOSING TRNXFILE' (:L865), 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' (:L882), 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTFILE' (:L898) and 'ERROR CLOSING ACCTFILE' (:L914); the four opens emit 'ERROR OPENING TRNXFILE' (:L739), 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE' (:L774), 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE' (:L792) and 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' (:L810). A single shared helper that composed 'ERROR ' plus a verb plus the DD name would reproduce all eight strings and would still be wrong the moment one of them was reached from the wrong paragraph, which is why the DD name in the emitted line is asserted here rather than the fact that some error line was emitted. This case pins the TRNXFILE close literal on the close site; the four ERROR OPENING literals are pinned by StatementGenerationJobATest.TheAbendPath.theFourOpenGuards, which drives a bad status at each of the four opens in turn from a @CsvSource of the four DD names, so all eight literals are covered between the two suites with nothing duplicated and nothing left unreached (gate G47). STATUS PROVENANCE - WHAT THE COLLABORATOR CAN LEGITIMATELY REPORT. CBSTM03B sets LK-M03B-RC by MOVE <ddname>FILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC at its four exits - :L152, :L176, :L201 and :L226 - so the value is a RAW TWO-CHARACTER COBOL FILE STATUS and each of the four DD names owns an INDEPENDENT status area. All four files are ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED and all four are opened OPEN INPUT, read-only, at :L136, :L160, :L184 and :L209; TRNXFILE (:L31-:L35) and XREFFILE (:L37-:L41) are ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL while CUSTFILE (:L43-:L47) and ACCTFILE (:L49-:L53) are ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM. The close itself is CLOSE TRNX-FILE at :L147, guarded by IF M03B-CLOSE, and control then falls to 1900-EXIT where the status is moved. '38' belongs to COBOL's 3x permanent-error family; the guard neither decodes it nor cares which member of that family arrives, because its only question is whether the two characters are '00' or '04' - so what this case pins is the ELSE arm and the verbatim rendering of an unaccepted status, not a claim about which physical condition produced it. The status is supplied by this case's declared scenario at the TRNXFILE close call site rather than by a seeded record, because a file status is a property of the environment and not of any row: no transaction record can be written that makes a healthy close report '38'. Note also MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC at :L859 - the figurative constant ZERO moved into a PIC X(02) receiver fills it with '0' characters, so the field reads '00' BEFORE the subroutine answers at all, and a collaborator that answered nothing whatever would be indistinguishable from one that closed cleanly. That is precisely why the status has to be substituted at the call site for this arm to be reachable at all. WHERE THE ABEND FALLS IN THE PROGRAM ORDER, AND WHAT THEREFORE NEVER RUNS. OPEN OUTPUT STMT-FILE HTML-FILE at :L293 and INITIALIZE WS-TRNX-TABLE WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR at :L294 run in the prologue, before anything is dispatched; the ALTER-driven chain at 0000-START (:L296-:L314) then opens all four inputs - 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN (:L730) with its own first read at :L746 and the 8500-READTRNX-READ load loop (:L818-:L853), then 8200-XREFFILE-OPEN (:L765), 8300-CUSTFILE-OPEN (:L783) and 8400-ACCTFILE-OPEN (:L801), whose GO TO 1000-MAINLINE at :L815 enters the record loop. The loop at :L317-:L329 runs to completion here: the single cross-reference row is read, the customer and the account are fetched, one statement is composed and its transactions are written, and the next cross-reference read reports '10' so END-OF-FILE becomes 'Y' and the PERFORM UNTIL leaves normally. Only then does :L331 PERFORM 9100-TRNXFILE-CLOSE - and that is where this case stops. EVERYTHING AFTER :L331 IS ASSERTED NOT TO RUN: 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE (:L333), 9300-CUSTFILE-CLOSE (:L335) and 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE (:L337) never execute, so 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' (:L882), 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTFILE' (:L898) and 'ERROR CLOSING ACCTFILE' (:L914) may not appear, and their absence from the ordered expectedMessages list is the assertion; CLOSE STMT-FILE HTML-FILE at :L339 never executes; and 9999-GOBACK at :L341 is never arrived at. Equally, this is the only abend case in which 1000-MAINLINE IS reached and a statement IS composed - case13, case14 and case15 all abend inside the loop before or during the first statement - so the accept arms of all five earlier guard sites it passes through are asserted here too, again by the absence of their literals: 'ERROR OPENING TRNXFILE' (:L739), 'ERROR READING TRNXFILE' (:L751 and :L844), 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE' (:L774), 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE' (:L792), 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' (:L810), 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' (:L359), 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' (:L383) and 'ERROR READING ACCTFILE' (:L407) are all absent, which says every one of those guards took its silent branch. THE TRUNCATION POINT, COUNTED FROM THE WRITE SEQUENCE AND NOT ESTIMATED (practice B11). The statement shape is 19 + N records on STMTFILE and 64 + 11N on HTMLFILE for N transactions, and every term is countable in the source: STMTFILE takes 16 records from 5000-CREATE-STATEMENT (WRITE FD-STMTFILE-REC FROM ST-LINE0 at :L460 plus the fifteen writes at :L488-:L502), 1 per transaction from 6000-WRITE-TRANS (ST-LINE14), and 3 from the 4000-TRNXFILE-GET footer at :L435-:L437; HTMLFILE takes 22 from 5100-WRITE-HTML-HEADER (:L509-:L552), 34 from 5200-WRITE-HTML-NMADBS (:L568-:L669), 11 per transaction from 6000-WRITE-TRANS, and 8 from the footer at :L440-:L454. This case seeds one cross-reference row and one transaction, so N is 1 and the counts are exactly 20 and 75 - the ninety-five images pinned below, every one of them complete. THE STMTFILE SEQUENCE, ROW BY ROW: row 0 is ST-LINE0's ALL '*' banner around 'START OF STATEMENT'; rows 1 to 4 are ST-LINE1 through ST-LINE4, the customer name 'Aniya Alba Von' and the three address lines; row 5 is the ST-LINE5 rule; row 6 is ST-LINE6's centred 'Basic Details'; row 7 is ST-LINE5 AGAIN (:L492 and :L494 are two separate writes of the same template); rows 8, 9 and 10 are ST-LINE7, ST-LINE8 and ST-LINE9 - 'Account ID         :00000000050', 'Current Balance    :000000492.00' and 'FICO Score         :623' with their interior space runs intact; row 11 is ST-LINE10's rule; row 12 is ST-LINE11's 'TRANSACTION SUMMARY '; row 13 is ST-LINE12's rule; row 14 is ST-LINE13's column headings; row 15 is ST-LINE12 a second time (:L500 then :L502); row 16 is the ST-LINE14 transaction line from 6000-WRITE-TRANS; row 17 is ST-LINE12 a THIRD time, now from the footer at :L435; row 18 is ST-LINE14A's 'Total EXP:' line; and row 19 is ST-LINE15's closing banner around 'END OF STATEMENT'. The three ST-LINE12 rows and the two ST-LINE5 rows are byte-identical eighty-character rules and are told apart by POSITION and never by content, which is why the row index is part of every expectation and why nothing is de-duplicated or reordered. The HTMLFILE sequence ends with the eight-record footer, so its last two rows are the '</body>' and '</html>' images at 100 bytes. THE TWO CHANNELS DISAGREE HERE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE CASE. expectedDatasets names STMTFILE with rowCount 20 at recordLength 80 and HTMLFILE with rowCount 75 at recordLength 100 on the WRITES channel - every record reached its sink, and the sinks were registered at :L293 before the first of them - and it names the SAME two datasets with rowCount 0 on the FINAL_STATE channel, because app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL declares STMTFILE DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE) at :L87 and HTMLFILE DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE) at :L92, and a run that does not reach :L339 and :L341 leaves NEITHER dataset behind however many records it wrote. Every other abend case in this program reports zero on both channels and therefore cannot tell the two apart; case01 completes and reports 20 and 75 on both. Only here do they differ, so only here does a translation that flushed its buffers on the way out of an abend, or that reported the retained rows as final state, or that treated an empty FINAL_STATE as licence to skip the WRITES assertion, actually fail. rowCount 0 is a positive assertion and not an absence of interest, and stating recordLength alongside it is the only way to pin the identity of a dataset expected to hold nothing: an empty eighty-byte statement file and an empty hundred-byte HTML file are not interchangeable just because both are empty. WIDTHS COME FROM TWO SOURCES EACH, AND ONE OF THEM IS A TRAP. STMTFILE is 80 bytes, from 01 FD-STMTFILE-REC PIC X(80) at :L45 and from CREASTMT.JCL LINE 89, DCB=(LRECL=80,BLKSIZE=8000,RECFM=FB), under the STMTFILE DD at line 87. LINE 90 OF THAT JCL IS GENUINELY CORRUPTED - verbatim '//         SPACE=(CYL,(1,1),RLSE), 00,RECFM=FB), ATA.VSAM.KSDS', a text-overlay artefact splicing fragments of other lines - and its ' 00,RECFM=FB)' remnant sits directly beneath STMTFILE where it is easily misread as LRECL=100. Line 89 is authoritative, and the JCL is left exactly as it stands: it is the parity oracle, so the hazard is recorded and worked around here rather than corrected there (practices B3 and B4 - app/cbl, app/cpy, app/jcl and app/data are read-only throughout). HTMLFILE is 100 bytes, from 01 FD-HTMLFILE-REC PIC X(100) at :L47 and from line 94, DCB=(LRECL=100,BLKSIZE=800,RECFM=FB), under the HTMLFILE DD at line 92; that SUPERSEDES STEP030's pre-delete declaration of LRECL=80,BLKSIZE=3200 at line 69, because the step that CREATES the dataset wins over the step that deletes it (gate G20, risk R-G). Both widths are asserted on both channels, and every one of the ninety-five expected images is exactly its dataset's width - eighty characters for each of the twenty statement rows and one hundred for each of the seventy-five HTML rows - which is what proves that every FILLER literal in the line templates was emitted rather than skipped, since a missing FILLER shortens the record and fails immediately (gates G19 and G21). SEEDS ARE REAL BYTES, AND THE INPUT IS PRESENT SO THAT ITS ABSENCE CANNOT BE THE EXPLANATION. XREFFILE is row 0 of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt verbatim - XREF-CARD-NUM 0500024453765740, XREF-CUST-ID 000000050, XREF-ACCT-ID 00000000050 - and it STAYS 36 BYTES here, exactly as shipped. ParityCase.Normalisation is the sole owner of the fourteen-space pad up to CVACT03Y's declared 50 - XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) plus XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) plus XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) plus FILLER X(14) - and applies it once, at seed time, through the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50, so the fixture is never edited and the pad is never double-applied (gates G16 and G21). ACCTFILE and CUSTFILE are acctdata.txt (300 x 50) and custdata.txt (500 x 50) whole. Both keyed reads take their keys from that one cross-reference row - 2000-CUSTFILE-GET with LENGTH OF XREF-CUST-ID = 9 at :L374 and 3000-ACCTFILE-GET with LENGTH OF XREF-ACCT-ID = 11 at :L398 - and both keys resolve, which is where every rendered value in the twenty statement rows comes from: the customer supplies 'Aniya Alba Von', '1588 Nienow Cape', 'Suite 187' and 'New OR USA 04257', and the account supplies 00000000050, a current balance of 492.00 and a FICO score of 623. The account row carries ACCT-CURR-BAL as the zoned span 00000004920{ - an S9(10)V99 field whose final byte is the sign overpunch, and '{' encodes a positive digit zero, so the digit string is 000000049200 and the value is 492.00 - which ST-CURR-BAL's PIC 9(9).99- renders as '000000492.00' followed by a blank sign position, nine integer digits and NOT zero-suppressed. The customer is read through CUSTREC, whose date of birth is CUST-DOB-YYYYMMDD and never CVCUS01Y's CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD; the two copybooks are near-identical and are deliberately kept as separate Java types so that field name survives (requirement I1). TRNXFILE IS INLINE BECAUSE THERE IS NO TENTH FIXTURE: app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine .txt files and none of them is a statement transaction file, so the single row is composed from app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY at EXACTLY 350 BYTES - TRNX-CARD-NUM X(16) plus TRNX-ID X(16) as the 32-byte composite key, which DELDEF01's IDCAMS corroborates with KEYS(32 0) and RECORDSIZE(350 350), then TRNX-REST as TRNX-TYPE-CD X(02) plus TRNX-CAT-CD 9(04) plus TRNX-SOURCE X(10) plus TRNX-DESC X(100) plus TRNX-AMT S9(09)V99 as 11 plus TRNX-MERCHANT-ID 9(09) plus TRNX-MERCHANT-NAME X(50) plus TRNX-MERCHANT-CITY X(50) plus TRNX-MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) plus TRNX-ORIG-TS X(26) plus TRNX-PROC-TS X(26) = 298, plus a trailing FILLER X(20) emitted as spaces = 318. The total width is what proves the FILLER was emitted at all (gate G21). Span by span the row is TRNX-CARD-NUM 0500024453765740, equal to the cross-reference card so that 4000-TRNXFILE-GET matches it at the 1-based WS-CARD-NUM(1); TRNX-ID TRAN000000000001; TRNX-TYPE-CD '01'; TRNX-CAT-CD '0001'; TRNX-SOURCE 'POS TERM  '; TRNX-DESC 'Written then discarded' padded to 100, which says in its own bytes what this case is about; TRNX-AMT '0000000990A', an 11-byte zoned S9(09)V99 whose final byte carries the sign, 'A' being the overpunch for a positive digit one, so the digit string is 00000009901 and the value is 99.01 and not 99.1 - the implied point falls two places from the right - which ST-TRANAMT's PIC Z(9).99- renders as '       99.01' with a blank sign position and which ST-TOTAL-TRAMT repeats after ADD TRNX-AMT TO WS-TOTAL-AMT at :L429 and MOVE WS-TRN-AMT TO ST-TOTAL-TRAMT at :L434; TRNX-MERCHANT-ID '000000001'; TRNX-MERCHANT-NAME 'Blick-Rippin' padded to 50; TRNX-MERCHANT-CITY 'Port Renayfurt' padded to 50; TRNX-MERCHANT-ZIP '60176     '; and two X(26) timestamps carrying the fixed 2022-07-18 12:00:00.000000 literal the shipped transaction data uses. Rows are ordered ascending by card then id, the order STEP010's SORT FIELDS=(263,16,CH,A,1,16,CH,A) produces; with one row that ordering is trivially satisfied and is stated so a later edit cannot quietly break it. Every amount in this migration is a BigDecimal at the declared scale with RoundingMode.DOWN - never HALF_UP, never HALF_EVEN, never double and never float - because the keyword ROUNDED appears zero times in all 28 programs. MESSAGES, ORDERED AND DERIVED LINE BY LINE: twelve DISPLAY_LINE expectations in emission order, and the order is part of the assertion. The first nine are the TIOT walk and nothing else - 'Running JCL : ' TIOTNJOB ' Step ' TIOTJSTP at :L270, with TIOTNJOB 'CREASTMT' and TIOTJSTP 'STEP040 ' eight bytes each, so that closing blank is the field's own and not decoration; 'DD Names from TIOT: ' at :L275; then one ': ' TIOCDDNM ' -- valid UCB' at :L279 for each of STEP040's six dataset DDs in JCL declaration order - TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, ACCTFILE, CUSTFILE, STMTFILE, HTMLFILE (CREASTMT.JCL lines 83 to 92; STEPLIB, SYSPRINT and SYSOUT at lines 80 to 82 are not data allocations, and ACCTFILE precedes CUSTFILE because the JCL declares it first); then the post-loop entry at :L290, whose ' -- null  UCB' carries TWO spaces after null and is byte-different from the in-loop ' --  null UCB' at :L281, with TIOCDDNM X(08) blank. The last three are the failure itself: 'ERROR CLOSING TRNXFILE' from :L865, then 'RETURN CODE: 38' from :L866 - the literal 'RETURN CODE: ' INCLUDING THE SPACE AFTER THE COLON, followed by WS-M03B-RC PIC X(02) rendered as exactly two characters with no padding and no numeric editing - and then 'ABENDING PROGRAM' from :L922, which the guard reaches by PERFORM. An implementation that emitted the code line before the verb line, that folded the two into one line, that trimmed the trailing space out of the prefix, or that formatted the status as a number rather than as the two characters the field holds, fails on this list rather than on a record. THE ABEND IS UNIQUE IN THE ESTATE AND STAYS THAT WAY (practice B5, gate G35). 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM at :L921 is exactly two statements: DISPLAY 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at :L922 and CALL 'CEE3ABD'. at :L923 - a BARE call with NO USING clause, therefore NO ABCODE and NO TIMING. Of the nine CALL 'CEE3ABD' sites across the twenty-eight programs this is the ONLY one shaped this way, and it is not normalised to match its eight siblings: in Java it becomes common.AbendException.withoutAbendParameters and not the standard() form that carries an abend code of 999 and a timing of 0. Because the DISPLAY precedes the call, 'ABENDING PROGRAM' is the LAST entry in expectedMessages rather than the first, and nothing at all follows it. THE RETURN CODE IS NOT FABRICATED (practice B1). expectedReturnCode is 8, and it comes from the abend convention alone. CBSTM03A CONTAINS NO MOVE STATEMENT ANYWHERE WHOSE RECEIVER IS RETURN-CODE - it declares no APPL-RESULT and no 88 APPL-EOF VALUE 16 either, and those belong to CBACT03C, CBACT04C, CBCUS01C, CBTRN01C and CBTRN02C rather than here - so the only non-zero exit this program has is the abend itself, and inventing an assignment to make the value look derived from the COBOL would be fabricating source that does not exist. 8 is AbendException.RETURN_CODE_ASSUMED_FAILURE, which StatementGenerationJobA names as its ABEND_RETURN_CODE and which is the code the estate's guarded sites carry for an assumed failure, sitting between the 4 of a warning and the 12 of an I/O error. The member is boxed and mandatory precisely so that an omitted key is refused rather than binding silently to 0: a case expecting an abend would otherwise have asserted a normal completion and passed. The value also matters downstream, because exactly three of CREASTMT.JCL's five steps carry COND=(0,NE) - STEP020, STEP030 and STEP040, while DELDEF01 and STEP010 carry none - so a non-zero code here is what would flush a following gated step, and case17 is the complementary case where this step is itself the one flushed. DETERMINISM AND ENCODING. Nothing here is read from a clock, a locale, a platform charset, a directory listing or an environment variable, so two runs of this case produce identical bytes (practice B7). The program composes no timestamp of its own; the two X(26) spans TRNX-ORIG-TS and TRNX-PROC-TS are inert seed bytes carrying the fixed 2022-07-18 12:00:00.000000 literal, and the TIOT job and step names are the constants CREASTMT and STEP040 taken from the JCL rather than from any runtime. Bytes are US-ASCII throughout, matching app/data/ASCII, and never a platform default (practice B8). PROVENANCE: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of the CBSTM03A and CBSTM03B paragraphs, cross-checked against the COSTM01, CVACT03Y, CUSTREC and CVACT01Y byte layouts, the CREASTMT.JCL DD, DCB and COND contracts, and the real ASCII fixtures. It was NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled and all four of this job's inputs are ORGANIZATION INDEXED, no Language Environment CEE* services exist so CEE3ABD itself could not be called, and app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy carries literal TAB characters on lines 6 to 22 that break parsing outright. That substitutes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else - twenty cases per program, field-for-field diffing, the diff-count-equals-zero gate per module and the branch-coverage bar all stand - and it is recorded rather than absorbed (practice B12, risk R-A). CASE ALLOCATION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY RENUMBERING (practice B4). The build prompt for this file described case16 as the four ERROR OPENING guards, driven one DD at a time. In the delivered suite that behaviour is pinned by StatementGenerationJobATest.TheAbendPath.theFourOpenGuards, a parameterised test whose @CsvSource carries all four DD names and their four literals, while CBSTM03AParityTest.scenario(String) pairs case16 with the TRNXFILE CLOSE call site and '38'. Four variants inside one case file are not expressible against the frozen contract: ParityCase carries NO member by which a BATCH_JOB case could inject a file status at all - forcedOutcomes belongs to ScreenRequest, which is legal only for a CONTROLLER_POJO - and a scenario names exactly one call site, which is why the status is an environmental property held beside the twenty case files rather than inside them. Renumbering to chase the prompt would either duplicate coverage that already exists at the four opens or leave 9100-TRNXFILE-CLOSE's ELSE arm - the only CLOSE guard any parity case in this program reaches - without a case at all, dropping it from gate G47. So the conflict is documented here and the substance is delivered in place, on the site the suite needs: the same '00' OR '04' guard shape that the four opens use, its byte-exact literal pair, the ordered three-line emission, the bare CEE3ABD abend and the return code it yields are every one of them pinned, and the four opens' own literals are covered by name in the sibling suite so that nothing in the estate is left unasserted.
